notes.meaning: Paul introduces himself as an apostle, a special messenger sent by Jesus Christ not by his own choice, but by the will of God. He writes to believers, calling them 'saints,' which means people who are set apart for God and dedicate themselves to him. These believers are faithful followers united in Jesus Christ.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: The earliest Greek manuscripts do not include the words 'in Ephesus,' indicating this letter may have been a circular letter sent to multiple churches across the region.

notes.meaning: Paul greets the church with God's grace and peace. Grace is God's free, undeserved favor and kindness, while peace is the deep sense of well-being that comes from being reconciled to him. Both gifts flow together from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul praises God, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, for blessing believers with every spiritual blessing. These blessings are not material riches, but heavenly gifts that secure our relationship with God in Christ. Because these blessings belong to the heavenly realms, nothing on earth can take them away.

God chose his people in Christ before he ever created the world. His goal in choosing them was that they should be holy, meaning set apart from sin, and blameless in his sight. His eternal plan flows entirely from his great love.

differ.view: God chose specific individual sinners before creation solely by his sovereign mercy, not based on any faith or good works he foresaw in them.
God chose from the beginning all people whom he foreknew would freely believe in Christ, electing believers as a group to share in salvation.

notes.meaning: God decided in advance to adopt believers as his own sons and daughters through Jesus Christ. In the ancient world, an adopted child gained full family rights and a fresh start, leaving behind old debts. God did not do this because of anything we earned, but simply because it pleased his will.

differ.view: God chose specific individuals before creation to be adopted into His family, based solely on His free mercy and grace rather than anything He foresaw in them. They teach that this choice is entirely God’s doing, so all praise belongs to Him alone.

God chose believers for salvation entirely by His grace in Christ before time began, without any human effort or choice. At the same time, Lutherans teach that God sincerely desires all people to be saved and predestined no one to be lost, accepting both truths together even though our human minds cannot fully solve the puzzle.

God does not pick certain people to be saved while leaving others out. Instead, God offers His saving love to all people, predestining the family gift of adoption for anyone who responds to His grace and places their faith in Christ.

notes.meaning: The ultimate goal of God's saving plan is that his glorious grace will be praised by all creation. He has freely showered this grace upon believers in his Beloved One, Jesus Christ. Because Jesus is fully accepted by the Father, everyone joined to him is fully accepted as well.

In Jesus, believers receive redemption, which means being bought back from slavery to sin and judgment. The ransom price was not silver or gold, but the blood that Jesus shed on the cross in his sacrificial death. This purchase brings complete forgiveness of all our sins according to the rich generosity of God's grace.

God did not hold back his grace, but poured it out abundantly on his people. In saving sinners, he showed perfect wisdom and understanding by satisfying his holy justice while offering full mercy. He also gives this understanding to believers so they may know and follow his ways.

God has made known the mystery of his will, which was once hidden in the past but is now revealed through the gospel. In the Bible, a mystery is not a puzzle people cannot solve, but a divine secret that God chooses to unveil. God chose to reveal this plan simply because it brought him delight to do so in Christ.

God planned history so that when the right time fully arrived, he would bring all things together under the authority of Christ. Sin brought division and disorder into creation, but God is restoring harmony to everything in heaven and on earth. Christ will reign over the whole universe as its supreme and rightful head.

In Christ, believers are chosen to receive God's promised inheritance of eternal life and glory. This outcome is not an accident, because God works out everything in the universe according to his wise purpose and plan. Christians can trust that God is always in sovereign control of his kingdom.

Paul points out that Jewish believers were the first to put their hope in the promised Messiah. God called them first so that their lives and salvation would bring glory and praise to his name. Their redemption proved that God is completely faithful to keep the promises he made to Israel.

Gentile believers were also brought into God's family when they heard the gospel of salvation and put their trust in Christ. At that point, God marked them as his own by giving them the Holy Spirit, like putting an official wax stamp of ownership on a document. This seal proves that they belong to God and are secure in him.

differ.view: Every person who puts faith in Jesus Christ is permanently sealed and indwelt by the Holy Spirit at the very moment they believe.
The sealing of the Holy Spirit is a distinct work of full assurance and inner transformation that often takes place after a person's initial conversion.

notes.meaning: The Holy Spirit inside believers is God's pledge, or first down payment, guaranteeing the full inheritance to come. This down payment gives Christians a taste of heaven until the final day when their bodies and souls are completely delivered from sin and death. This final rescue will bring everlasting praise to God's glory.

Paul writes that he has heard reports of how the Ephesians are living out the Christian life. He singles out two clear signs of true faith: their unwavering trust in the Lord Jesus and their active love for all of God's people. Genuine faith in Christ always overflows into practical love for other believers.

Because Paul sees the fruit of their faith, he never stops thanking God for them whenever he prays. He shows that Christian love leads believers to bring one another before God regularly. Even healthy and faithful churches still need continual prayer to keep growing.

Paul prays that God the Father will give believers the Spirit of wisdom and revelation. He is not asking for strange new doctrines, but for a deeper, personal relationship with God. True spiritual wisdom helps believers know God himself more intimately every day.

Paul asks God to enlighten the eyes of their hearts, which means giving spiritual understanding to their inner minds and desires. With clear spiritual sight, believers can understand the bright hope God has called them to receive. They also discover how precious and rich God's chosen people are to him as his own treasured inheritance.

Paul wants Christians to grasp how enormously great God's power is toward those who believe. This is not a distant, dormant strength, but active energy at work inside believers to sustain their faith. The very same power that rules the universe is currently helping Christians in their daily walk.

God proved this extraordinary power when he brought Jesus back from the dead. After the resurrection, God seated Jesus at his right hand in the heavenly realms, which is the highest place of honor, authority, and rule. The resurrection shows that God's power has conquered even the grave.

Jesus is seated far above every ruler, authority, power, and dominion in existence. This includes all earthly kings, human governments, and every rank of angel or demon. His supreme name and authority rule not only in this present world, but will continue without end in the world to come.

God put everything in complete subjection under Christ's feet, picturing an ancient king stepping on the necks of defeated enemies. God then gave this victorious Ruler to be the head over all things for the benefit of the church. Because Jesus controls the entire universe, his people are completely safe under his leadership.

Paul explains that the church is the body of Christ, closely joined to him as its living head. Just as a physical body receives its life, direction, and strength from the head, believers receive everything from Jesus. The church serves as the visible fullness of Christ, who fills the entire universe with his presence and power.
